items.title: Akiyoshi Toshiko — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Great writing came from Jaki Byard—boy, he could write! And uh, it was a very exciting band, so I used to listen, every Monday night they played and I used to listen to that.

ctx.x: Who were some of the other students that you were in classes with? You mentioned several profe—, uh, teachers….

Yes. Gene Cherico. He was, he had a natural ear. He used to be a drummer. And when he was in the service he got in a car accident that hit a train, and he almost lost his life. So anyway, he, the arm, the surgeon took a bone from [his] hip and replaced the arm, and he suggested he play the bass, pull the bass, to help [recover]. That‟s how he became a bass player. So, I‟m not saying because of that, but he had a natural beat, he was really a … you know, but he had a tremendous ear. He didn‟t know much about…
Was there a piano teacher there or…?
